---
title: "Code structure"
guide-section: "Reference"
---

This page shows which functions call which. The trees below come from
[`callgrove`](https://mjfrigaard.github.io/callgrove/). It reads the
package source without running the app. Each cell runs on every docs
build, so the trees always match the code.

```{python}
from pathlib import Path

import baseball_trajectory
from callgrove import call_tree_app, call_tree_dir

pkg = Path(baseball_trajectory.__file__).parent
```

## The server

`call_tree_dir()` parses every `.py` file in the package and builds the
tree from one function. Here it starts at `server()` in `app.py`:

```{python}
call_tree_dir(pkg, root="server")
```

A node with children starts with `█─`. Each `server.` node is a reactive
function inside `server()`, such as an `@reactive.effect` or a
`@render.plot`. The tree shows where each one reaches into the other
modules:

* The search effects call `search_player()` in `data.py`.
* `career_df` calls `get_batting_career()` or `get_pitching_career()`.
* `trajectory_plot` fits the curve and draws the chart.
* `summary_table` calls `summarize_career()`.

Helpers defined inside `server()` show up under each function that calls
them. `_weight_col()` picks PA or IP for the Position toggle, so it
appears as `server._weight_col` under `career_df`, `trajectory_plot`,
and `summary_table`. A helper defined inside a render function carries
both names: `server.summary_table._round2`.

## Imports and aliases

`app.py` reaches the other modules in several ways. `callgrove` follows
each one back to the function it names:

| Call in `app.py` | Import | Function |
|---|---|---|
| `mdl.is_lower_better()` | `import baseball_trajectory.model as mdl` | `model.is_lower_better()` |
| `plots.plot_trajectory()` | `from . import plots` | `plots.plot_trajectory()` |
| `summarize()` | `from .model import summarize_career as summarize` | `model.summarize_career()` |
| `_model.fit()` | `_model = CareerModel()` at the top of `app.py` | `model.CareerModel.fit()` |

Each node is labeled with the name of the definition, not the alias, so
`summarize()` shows as `summarize_career` and `_model.fit()` shows as
`CareerModel.fit`.

## The model class

`CareerModel` wraps `fit_player_curve()`. It returns `None` when a player
has fewer than `min_seasons` qualifying seasons (default 3). The app
keeps one shared instance, `_model`, and `summarize_career()` builds its
own:

```{python}
call_tree_dir(pkg, root="summarize_career")
```

`CareerModel.__init__` only stores `min_seasons`, so it has no children.
`CareerModel.fit` counts the seasons with `_n_seasons()`, then calls
`fit_player_curve()`.

## The running app

`call_tree_app()` starts from the `App` object instead of the files. It
reads the server function and looks up each name the way the server
sees it:

```{python}
#| warning: false
from baseball_trajectory.app import app

call_tree_app(app)
```

Below the `app` root, the tree matches the one from `call_tree_dir()`,
labels included. Reading the files and reading the running app give the
same answer.

The app's UI is built when `App()` is created, so `call_tree_app()` has
no UI function to follow. The tree only has the server branch.
